item.title: The Wrong Valley: Twenty Minutes at Balaclava
item.description:
Recounts how, on the plain of Balaclava in the Crimea on the twenty-fifth of October, eighteen fifty-four, a hastily written four-line order from Lord Raglan was misread as it passed down the chain of command, and the British Light Brigade was sent down the North Valley, exposed to artillery fire from three sides. The episode ranges from the two small victories of that same morning to the death of Captain Nolan, who carried the order, by the first shell, and from the way the blame was laid on a dead man afterwards to how the disaster was turned into a triumph by Tennyson's lines.
Konular: crimean war, balaclava, light brigade, 1854, military history.

item.title: Baler: The Last Soldiers of a Finished War
item.description:
Recounts how a Spanish detachment of some fifty men barricaded themselves inside the church of Baler in the Philippines on the first of July, eighteen ninety-eight, and held out for three hundred and thirty-seven days without accepting that Spain had lost the war and surrendered the islands. The episode ranges from beriberi, desertion and the officers who died inside the church to the newspapers the defenders dismissed as forgeries, and to Aguinaldo's decree that sent them home not as prisoners but as sons
Konular: baler, spanish-american war, philippines, siege, 1898.

item.title: Uldolmok: The Fleet Stopped by Thirteen Ships
item.description:
Tells how the Korean admiral Yi Sun-sin, stripped of rank on a slander and put to torture in fifteen ninety-seven, held off hundreds of Japanese ships in the Uldolmok Strait with the thirteen vessels left after the fleet was destroyed at Chilcheollyang. The episode covers how the strait's tidal current was turned into a weapon, and the last order the admiral gave a year later at Noryang.
Konular: yi sun-sin, myeongnyang, korea, imjin war, naval battle.

item.title: A Handful of Peppercorns: The Cannons Istanbul Sent to Sumatra
item.description:
Tells how the Aceh Sultanate in Sumatra asked Istanbul for help against Portugal in the fifteen sixties, how the envoys who arrived with a shipload of black pepper were kept waiting at the palace for a year, and how the gunners, founders and engineers dispatched by Selim the Second established the Ottomans' easternmost military reach. The episode ranges from the fleet diverted from its course by the revolt in Yemen to Kurtoğlu Hızır Reis's voyage of fifteen sixty-eight to fifteen sixty-nine, the giant cannons cast in Aceh, and the failure of the siege of Malacca.
Konular: ottoman, aceh, portugal, indian ocean, malacca.

item.title: The Peacock Throne: The Shah Who Emptied Delhi
item.description:
Tells how the Persian ruler Nadir Shah scattered the Mughal army at Karnal in seventeen thirty-nine in a matter of hours, then entered Delhi, sacked the city, and carried off a treasure that included the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor. The episode covers how that single campaign turned the Mughal Empire into a hollow shell and opened India to new masters.
Konular: nadir shah, mughal empire, battle of karnal, peacock throne, koh-i-noor.

item.title: Talas 751: The Captives Who Carried Paper West
item.description:
Tells of the single encounter between Tang China and the newly founded Abbasid Caliphate on the banks of the Talas River, on today's Kyrgyzstan–Kazakhstan border, in July seven hundred and fifty-one, and how the Tang army fell apart when the Karluks changed sides in the middle of the fight. The episode follows the Chinese artisans taken captive to trace how papermaking travelled to Samarkand and Baghdad, asks how much of that account is true, and covers the Tang withdrawal from Central Asia.
Konular: battle of talas, tang dynasty, abbasids, karluks, history of paper.

item.title: The Winter War: Soviet Divisions Swallowed by the Snow
item.description:
Recounts the Soviet Union's attack on Finland on the thirtieth of November, nineteen thirty-nine, and the resistance put up for one hundred and five days by a country fifty times smaller in population. The episode ranges from the Soviet divisions torn apart in the snow at Suomussalmi and on the Raate Road to the Moscow Peace, and to the way the weakness displayed by the Red Army emboldened Hitler toward Barbarossa.
Konular: winter war, finland, soviet union, motti tactic, mannerheim line.

item.title: The Ten Thousand: An Army Stranded Inside Persia
item.description:
Tells how the more than ten thousand Greek mercenaries hired by Cyrus the Younger to take the Persian throne from his brother in four hundred and one BC were left leaderless and friendless in the very heart of the empire when Cyrus died at Cunaxa, and how they marched fifteen hundred miles back to the Black Sea. The episode ranges from the ambush and killing of the generals at a banquet to Xenophon's election to command, from the winter crossing of the Anatolian mountains to the way this march exposed Persian weakness to the Greek world.
Konular: ancient greece, persian empire, xenophon, ten thousand, mercenaries.
